_meta.primary_evidence: Fatima's own drupal.org contributor profile (Wayback 20190930224616) lists her Sessions, Scholarship years, and events attended. This is the strongest primary source for the Drupal-era speaking record and is used to settle the Vienna question.

resolutions.recommendation: QUARANTINE the existing content-db entry drupalcon-vienna-2017-imposter (pending Fatima confirmation per quarantine rules).
resolutions.finding: Fatima's own drupal.org contributor profile is decisive. Under 'Sessions' it names ONLY: DrupalCon Nashville (OOP the Pokemon Journey + 2 Community Convos) and DrupalCon Baltimore (The Imposter Monologues part II). It does NOT list any DrupalCon Vienna session. Separately, the profile lists Vienna 2017 under 'Scholarship recipient' and under Drupal events attended. Conclusion: Fatima ATTENDED DrupalCon Vienna 2017 on scholarship but there is no public evidence she was a PANELIST on 'The Imposter Monologues, Vol. 3'. The Vienna session page (events.drupal.org, confirmed via Wayback 20231211123303 + 20250826105431, identical digest) carries only a generic panel description with no named speaker list. Rachel Lawson's retrospective (rachelnorfolk.me) confirms Lawson herself was a panelist and embeds a @sugaroverflow tweet from the same conference, but does not place Fatima on the panel. The most likely origin of the content-db Vienna entry is conflation with the confirmed Baltimore 'part II' appearance.
resolutions.curator_note: Do NOT resurrect without Fatima's explicit confirmation. If Fatima recalls actually being on the Vienna panel, treat as personal-record-only and note that the public event page did not name any panelists.

resolutions.finding: DATE RESOLVED. The events.drupal.org North America 2021 speakers page (indexed 2021-04-13) groups the 'Fireside chat: JavaScript ate the Web' session with Friday, 16 April programming, confirming the Friday-16-April reading over the earlier Wednesday-14 guess. Conference ran virtually April 12-16, 2021, 11:00am-3:00pm Eastern (UTC-5) per events.drupal.org/drupalcon2021/news/lead-session and drupal.regfox.com/drupalcon-north-america-2021. Panel + title + role independently corroborated by TWO sources: (a) events.drupal.org NA-2021 wrap-up page names 'Fireside chat with Sally Young, Fatima Sarah Khalid, and Ben Morss - JavaScript ate the Web: Key lessons for the Drupal community'; (b) Pantheon blog recap (pantheon.io/blog/drupalcon-2021-session-recap) names the same lineup, moderator Steve Persch, and Fatima's then-title 'Developer Programs Engineer' at Pantheon.
resolutions.recommendation: Merge as NET-NEW with date '2021-04-16' and verification_status 'verified-live'. Title: 'JavaScript ate the Web: Key lessons for the Drupal community' (fireside chat / panel). Co-panelists Sally Young + Ben Morss, moderated by Steve Persch (Pantheon).
resolutions.curator_note: Date settled to Fri 16 Apr 2021 via events.drupal.org speakers page grouping (session listed with Friday 16 April programming) + Pantheon recap. Two independent corroborating sources for panel/title/role. No remaining ambiguity on this entry.

resolutions.finding: The actual ATO 2022 session title is recovered from a primary source. The All Things Open 'Community Track Recordings Now live!' post (allthingsopen.org/community-track-recordings-now-live, published 2022-12-19) lists: 'Lessons Learned Leading an OSS Diversity Team — Fatima Sarah Khalid, GitLab' with a Watch Recording link. This upgrades the entry from generic 'speaker appearance' to a concrete, source-supported talk title with a recording.
resolutions.recommendation: Merge as an update to existing content-db all-things-open-2022 (currently quarantined as 'title TBC'). Now has a real title and is eligible to leave quarantine pending Fatima confirmation. Set title to 'Lessons Learned Leading an OSS Diversity Team', type 'talk', affiliation gitlab.

The RESEARCH-SCOPE draft guessed 'DEI Track Chair 2018'; the profile-supported title is TRACK CHAIR for the 'Building Community' track at DrupalCon Nashville 2018. Use the profile wording, not the scope-doc guess.

drupal.org profile describes her as on the 'Leadership team Drupal Diversity & Inclusion working group' and 'Leader of the Drupal Diversity & Inclusion working group.' CV says 'Team Lead' 2017-2019. All three phrasings agree on a leadership role; recommend 'Team Lead' per CV, note the drupal.org corroboration.
